whole_row.py _is_exempt (118-123) exempts a star that is the COUNT argument (COUNT(*), COUNT(t.*)) and any star under exp.Exists. _expands_table (126-143) refuses unless every source is non-Table: a qualified t.* checks only its own source, a bare * checks all selected_sources, and an unresolved qualifier or scope is refused. CTE, derived table, VALUES, UNNEST and LATERAL sources are Scope or non-Table nodes, so they are allowed. _is_stored_relation (146-150) allows table functions and is_catalog_table relations. Any other Table is refused. A star over a CTE that itself stars a table is refused at the inner star. A bare * joining a table and a CTE is refused, because any stored source triggers it. I found no input where a star expanding a table or view escapes. This matches the config.py description.

docs/external/configuration.md:32 matches whole_row.py. _whole_row_star/_expands_table (lines 100-143) refuse any non-exempt star whose select source is an exp.Table that is a stored relation (_is_stored_relation, 146-150, excludes table functions and catalogs via is_catalog_table). _is_exempt (118-123) allows COUNT(*)/COUNT(t.*) and any star inside EXISTS. A star over a CTE/derived table (source is a Scope, not exp.Table) is allowed, while a star inside a CTE or subquery that reads a table is checked in its own Select scope via statement.find_all(exp.Star), so it is refused even if the outer query names columns. Catalog tables are allowed. row_to_json(t) has no exp.Star so it is not caught (module docstring lines 32-34). Hostile input traced: WITH c AS (SELECT * FROM t) SELECT a FROM c. The inner star's scope has a Table source, so it is refused, as the doc says. Verified true: WholeRowSelectError(UnsafeSqlError) at whole_row.py:80; WHOLE_ROW_REFUSAL keeps 'selects every column' (whole_row.py:72-77); WholeRowSelectGuardRunner re-raises with 'refusing to execute query: ' prefix (176); RunSqlTool catches Exception and returns success=False with 'Error executing query: {e}' (agent/tools/run_sql.py:197-201); query_database.py:673 has the UnsafeSqlError branch. Not true as an absolute: 'naming the star ... but no table'. The star text is node.sql() of the Column (whole_row.py:113-114, 97), so for an unaliased qualified star, e.g. SELECT users.* FROM users, the message contains '(users.*)', which names the table. The 'TABLE t' path also yields '(TABLE)'. Doc sentence at read-only-safety.md:214 is therefore overstated: the qualifier is echoed, and it is a table name when not aliased.

(1) _parse_statements (readonly.py:571-586) wraps ParseError/TokenError into UnsafeSqlError. _mysql_parse_sql (readonly.py:511-561) raises UnsafeSqlError for ambiguous MySQL input such as executable comments, nested comments, double-dash ambiguity and backslash quotes. (2) _whole_row_star (whole_row.py:102-108) returns early unless some star is non-exempt, and only after that calls normalize_identifiers and traverse_scope. A query with no star, or only exempt stars, never reaches them. Hostile input checked: COUNT(*)-only query returns None at line 103 before either call. WholeRowSelectError subclasses UnsafeSqlError but is caught by the earlier clause only if raised inside assert_no_whole_row_select, which does not apply to unexpected exceptions.

whole_row.py:90 calls first_sql_keyword(sql, dialect) positionally; signature at readonly.py:45 is (sql, dialect=None). It tokenizes via sqlglot (comments attach to tokens, not emitted as tokens), skips L_PAREN, and returns token.text.upper() for VAR or keyword tokens (readonly.py:76-83), so 'TABLE users' and '/* note */ table users' give 'TABLE' (TABLE is a word keyword mapped to its own token type in KEYWORDS). Read installed sqlglot 30.27.0 (satisfies pyproject pin >=30.22,<31) optimizer/normalize_identifiers.py: signature normalize_identifiers(expression, dialect=None, ...) and Dialect.get_or_raise(dialect) accepts None (line 66). It walks the given tree and calls dialect.normalize_identifier(node) (line 99), which does expression.set('this', ...) in place (dialect.py:1190), then returns the same expression (line 101). So discarding the result at whole_row.py:107 is safe. Caveat: in this version nodes are mutated rather than replaced, so 'nodes may be replaced' is a conservative allowance, not observed behavior; the code at whole_row.py:108-109 re-collects stars after normalization, which is correct either way.

Installed sqlglot scope.py: TRAVERSABLES = (exp.Query, exp.DDL, exp.DML) (line 20), so traverse_scope (703) accepts CREATE/INSERT roots. _traverse_scope: DDL branch (739-744) builds Scope(ddl_expression) for the inner Query and yields it, so scope.expression is the inner Select node itself; DML branch (745-788) scopes queries found in the statement via Scope(query)/scope.branch(query), again rooted on the actual node. SetOperation (UNION) scopes are yielded too, with branch Selects scoped separately. So id(scope.expression) lookups in whole_row.py:108/127-128 resolve a star's enclosing Select. Caveat: the version read is the hosted-toolcache one, not a pinned lockfile copy.

Installed sqlglot scope.py:439-464: selected_sources is dict[str, tuple[exp.Selectable, exp.Table | Scope]]; result[name] = (node, self.sources[name]), a 2-tuple whose second element is an exp.Table or a Scope (a nested scope object, not a raw expression; the claim's 'scope/subquery' wording covers this loosely). Keys are reference names (alias_or_name) taken from the statement after normalize_identifiers(statement) at whole_row.py:107, so they have the same case as column.table qualifiers, which are normalized in the same pass. The code at whole_row.py:134-141 uses entry[1] and isinstance(source, exp.Table), consistent with this.

whole_row.py:100-143: _whole_row_star walks every exp.Star via find_all (any position: projection, CTE, derived table, IN/scalar subquery, function argument). _expands_table (126-143) uses the nearest enclosing Select; if no scope resolves, or a qualified t.* has no matching source, it returns True (refused, fail closed). Otherwise it refuses when any (or the named) source is a stored Table not a catalog or table function (146-150). Only exemptions are COUNT and EXISTS (118-123), plus the documented CTE/derived/VALUES/function sources. Traced a hostile input: row_to_json(t.*) in a nested subquery resolves to its nearest Select scope with a Table source, so it is refused. Union branches and subqueries have their own Select scopes. I found no star position that returns False for a stored table outside the documented exemptions. I did not run the code.

whole_row.py:102-103 returns None before normalize_identifiers (107) and traverse_scope (108) unless some star in the statement is non-exempt. The check is per statement (assert_no_whole_row_select loops at 92-97). A multi-statement input whose second statement has no non-exempt star returns early for that statement, and a query with no non-exempt star in any statement never reaches either call. _is_exempt (118-123) uses only parent checks and find_ancestor, which walks parent pointers and needs neither normalization nor scope analysis, so it does not break the claim. Normalization and scope analysis are called only in _whole_row_star after the guard.

whole_row.py:90-97 checks first_sql_keyword()==TABLE only on the leading keyword, then loops over _parse_statements(); None statements (readonly.py:571-586 returns sqlglot.parse output, which can contain None for empty statements) are skipped at line 93-94, which is harmless since they hold no star. The open question is a later statement such as 'SELECT 1; TABLE t'. The leading-keyword check does not see it, and the star walk finds no exp.Star unless sqlglot parses 'TABLE t' into a star-bearing tree. The module docstring (lines 28-30) and the test at tests/unit/test_safety_whole_row.py:152 say sqlglot does not parse it as SELECT *. If sqlglot parses it without error, the docstring claim 'every statement ... whatever its kind' is false for a non-first TABLE statement. If sqlglot raises ParseError, it is refused. I did not run sqlglot.parse('SELECT 1; TABLE t'), so this is not settled. The test file has no multi-statement TABLE case.

factory.py:85-101 builds engine runner -> RowCapRunner -> ReadOnlyGuardRunner -> RlsGuardRunner; WholeRowSelectGuardRunner is applied last at factory.py:126-127, outermost. Grep shows factory.py:127 is the only construction site of WholeRowSelectGuardRunner, so no shipped path puts it between RlsGuardRunner and the relation-verifying runner; RlsGuardRunner is always outside it, so _relation_check_executor (safety/__init__.py:240) only needs to unwrap RlsGuardRunner/ReadOnlyGuardRunner/RowCapRunner. Fail-closed: whole_row.py:179-188 catches Exception and raises WholeRowSelectError before calling inner.run_sql. A BaseException such as KeyboardInterrupt is not caught by except Exception, but it propagates out of run_sql before line 190, so the query is still not executed (refused). The claim holds.

The allowances are accurate: _is_exempt (whole_row.py:118-123) exempts COUNT(*) and any star inside EXISTS, and _expands_table (126-143) only flags stars over stored relations, so a star over a CTE or derived table is allowed. The last sentence, 'Whole tables cannot be exported through this tool.' (whole_row.py:76), is an absolute claim that the code does not back. The module docstring (32-34) says 'Not covered: a whole row reached without a star, such as row_to_json(t) or a bare t as a composite value, and an explicit list of every column.' So 'SELECT a,b,c FROM t' listing every column, or PostgreSQL 'SELECT row_to_json(t) FROM t', passes the guard and returns the whole table through run_sql. The guard only blocks star expansion. Other tools in src/sqllens/agent/tools (agent_memory, emit_chart, emit_text, run_sql) are not export paths, so the counterexample comes from run_sql itself. The refusal text overstates the guarantee and contradicts the file's own docstring. The effect is small because it is guidance text shown to the agent.
